messages:
Camille: Heads-up team — I put together a compact 12-minute 'dry-run + safety net' runbook for LuminaHealth's renewal demo next Wed. Goal: make the demo deterministic, avoid tail spikes, and have a clear rollback + feedback capture flow. Pasting below for edits.

Omar: Love the safety-net angle. Can we add an explicit "customer consent" blurb for automated fallback so they understand what changes when we switch models?

Nisha: Yep. Also suggest we include a one-click repro link for the support console so CS can paste metrics on the call.

Camille: Runbook (12 minutes total):
1) Intro and consent (1m) — confirm success criteria and read this script to the customer: "If we face prolonged latency we'll temporarily switch to a faster model variant to keep replies available. This preserves uptime but may alter phrasing; we will log differences and follow up with recommended prompt tweaks and remediation."
2) Deterministic warm-up (3m) — send 8 exact demo prompts (3 short, 3 medium, 2 long) to prime KV and batch lanes. Note: use the exact demo phrasing to maximize cache hits.
3) Micro-batch exercise (2m) — trigger 4 parallel requests to exercise batching lanes and surface queueing behavior.
4) Tail-probe & quick fix (2m) — run the p99 probe, if p99 > threshold trigger the pre-approved rollback sequence.
5) Failover demo (2m) — toggle to fallback model and show Console banner; explain tradeoffs.
6) Feedback capture & commit (2m) — fill the post-demo feedback form together and confirm owners for regressions.

Vik: Rollback sequence (one-liner to paste in ops playbook):
```bash
# immediate rollback: switch routing for tenant -> smaller-model and revoke canary
curl -X POST $CONTROL/api/tenants/lumina/routing -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" -d '{"route_override":"open-3b","reason":"demo-rollback"}'
# notify CS channel
curl -X POST $SLACK_WEBHOOK -d '{"text":"Rollback executed for LuminaHealth demo - SRE oncall informed."}'
```

Omar: Probe one-liner for the call (paste into support shell):
```bash
python tools/latency_probe.py --tenant lumina --model open-7b --samples 24 --json | jq -r '.summary | "p50:\(.p50) p95:\(.p95) p99:\(.p99) kv_hit:\(.kv_hit)"'
```

Nisha: Feedback capture: use this short form during the call so we can triage quickly: https://forms.redwood.example/f/lumina-demo-feedback (fields: perceived latency, phrasing-regression? yes/no, severity, sample example). CS should copy one example if quality is flagged.

Camille: Customer-facing consent blurb added to invite. Also adding a short "what we'll do if quality drops" script: read verbatim and confirm their OK before proceeding.

ops-bot: [deploy] LuminaHealth canary: last deploy 2026-02-20T10:22:11Z. No incidents.

Vik: Ops tips for the live call: keep Console > Per-route open, have the routing override command ready in a terminal, pre-label logs with tenant=lumina-demo for 60m: `kubectl label pods -n prod tenant=lumina-demo=true --overwrite`. Also keep a staged fallback model warmed in staging.

Omar: I'll attach the warmup prompt set and token-estimates to the invite and include a short note about token cost for warmup (~300-800 tokens).

Nisha: I'll prepare the repro link to the support console and the short feedback form as a fallback capture.

Camille: Thanks — owners: Omar (prompts + token est), Vik (rollback rehearsals + labels), Nisha (feedback form + repro link). I'll paste the runbook & customer consent into the calendar invite now. :thumbsup:
